ded Inventory.commit(sku, qty) to convert a reservation into an actual deduction of on-hand stock (checks reserved and on-hand).
  - Kept reports that iterate inventory.stock unchanged so they still use on-hand quantities.

- orders.py
  - create_order now attempts to reserve all items. If any reservation fails, it rolls back any previous reservations and re-raises (so InsufficientStock is raised and nothing is created or reserved).
  - cancel releases reservations for pending orders before marking the order cancelled.
  - fulfill converts reservations to actual on-hand deductions by calling Inventory.commit for each line.

Tests
- Ran the test suite (unittest) — all tests pass locally: 5 tests OK.

Notes and assumptions
- create_order raises InsufficientStock when reservation fails (per your instruction). Validation errors for empty or zero quantities still raise OrderError.
- The reservation logic is not thread-safe; if this system needs to be concurrent, we should add locking around reservation/commit/release operations.
- Reports low_stock and stock_value continue to use inventory.stock (on-hand) as requested.

If you want, I can:
1. Add new tests explicitly asserting reservation behavior (e.g., available immediately drops after create_order, cancel restores available).
2. Add basic thread-safety (a lock) around Inventory methods.
3. Return more user-friendly error types/messages or propagate InsufficientStock as OrderError when creating an order (if you prefer that API).
